gate_1_block.claim: a block on an incline sticks for tan(theta) <= mu and slides at g (sin(theta) - mu cos(theta)) past it, at 0.5, 0.9995, 1.0005 and 2 of breakaway, both dtypes

prediction.why: two rims held on a flat, each a single-point problem solved exactly in one sweep; the spike's four-corner box needed 200 sweeps near breakaway, two rims along the slope couple less [inference]

control.plant: mu doubled: a slope of tan(theta) = 1.5 mu slides at mu and sticks at 2 mu

gate_1_block.if_wrong: if the block creeps near breakaway, the two rims' coupling needs more sweeps: the residual and the sweep count say how many
gate_1_block.cannot_discriminate_if: the threshold's two sides are both on one branch

gate_2_sphere_node.claim: a solid sphere on the node's plane rolls without slipping at (5/7) g sin(theta) for tan(theta) <= (7/2) mu, and slips past it with its spin at (5/2) mu g cos(theta) / a, either side of the threshold

prediction.why: a sphere's sliding pair and its normal row decouple (the code read's -0.845 is rolling resistance's, not built here)

control.plant: frictionless: the sphere slides at g sin(theta) and never turns

gate_3_sphere_build.claim: the same through built.run on a tilted tube's floor (the contact's default margin, the roughness cutoff)

gate_4_ledger.claim: friction's loss under its own name is mu N times the slip distance while it slides and zero while it rolls; no gift step; the books close

prediction.unit: |loss - mu N sum(dt |slip|)| / max(expected, m g 1 mm)
prediction.why: friction is booked -dt |l| |u| at the solved slip; sliding |l| = mu N

control.plant: friction's sign flipped (disk_update returns -x): the power guard trips and the numerical column carries -2 dt |l||u|

gate_5_gradients.claim: reverse mode in mu through the run equals the closed form sliding (-g cos(theta) T) and central differences (float64); zero rolling (cannot discriminate there: the trajectory does not depend on mu above its threshold)
